\chapter{Chapter06 — Small Bias Output Bit}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from FABL.Chapter06.Constructions.SmallBiasOutputBit
\section{Overview}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{FABL.Chapter06.Constructions.SmallBiasOutputBit}.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Binary dot product state]
\lean{FABL.executableBinaryDotProductState}
\label{FABL.executableBinaryDotProductState}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.binaryCoefficientAt, FABL.𝔽₂}
For two binary vectors $a,b$ of length $\ell$ and each natural number $k$, define a state
recursively by $S_0=0$ and $S_{k+1}=S_k+a_kb_k$, where a coefficient at an index outside
the vectors' range is interpreted as zero.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Binary dot product]
\lean{FABL.executableBinaryDotProduct}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p034-b002}
\label{FABL.executableBinaryDotProduct}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.executableBinaryDotProductState, FABL.𝔽₂}
For a natural number $\ell$ and vectors $a,b\in(\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z})^\ell$, define
their executable binary dot product to be the value returned by the specified
state-based computation on $a$, $b$, and $\ell$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Recursive dot product state as a sum]
\lean{FABL.executableBinaryDotProductState_eq_sum}
\label{FABL.executableBinaryDotProductState_eq_sum}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.binaryCoefficientAt, FABL.executableBinaryDotProductState}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\mathbb{F}_2$ be the field with two elements, let $\ell$ be a nonnegative integer,
and let $a,b\in\mathbb{F}_2^\ell$. For every nonnegative integer $k$, the recursive dot
product state after $k$ steps equals $\sum_{j=0}^{k-1} a_jb_j$, where a coordinate with
index at least $\ell$ is interpreted as zero.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Executable binary dot product]
\lean{FABL.executableBinaryDotProduct_eq_f₂DotProduct}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.binaryCoefficientAt, FABL.executableBinaryDotProduct, FABL.executableBinaryDotProductState_eq_sum, FABL.f₂DotProduct}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\ell$ be a nonnegative integer and let $a,b\in\mathbb{F}_2^\ell$, where
$\mathbb{F}_2$ is the field with two elements. The executable binary dot product of $a$
and $b$ equals their dot product over $\mathbb{F}_2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Small bias output bit]
\lean{FABL.executableSmallBiasOutputBit}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p153-b003}
\label{FABL.executableSmallBiasOutputBit}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CertifiedBinaryFieldImplementation, FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.binaryPowMod, FABL.executableBinaryDotProduct, FABL.𝔽₂}
Let $\ell>0$, let a certified binary field implementation of degree $\ell$ be given, and
choose vectors $r,s\in(\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z})^\ell$. For $i\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, define
the output bit as the binary dot product of $s$ with the $i+1$-st power of $r$ modulo
the implementation's monic irreducible polynomial.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Output bit agrees with generator coordinate]
\lean{FABL.executableSmallBiasOutputBit_eq_generator}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p153-b003}
\label{FABL.executableSmallBiasOutputBit_eq_generator}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CertifiedBinaryFieldImplementation, FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.executableBinaryDotProduct_eq_f₂DotProduct, FABL.executableSmallBiasGenerator, FABL.executableSmallBiasOutputBit}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n,\ell\in\mathbb N$, with $\ell>0$, and let a certified binary field implementation
of degree $\ell$ and binary vectors $r,s$ of length $\ell$ be given. For every $i<n$,
the output bit at coordinate $i$ equals coordinate $i$ of the generator vector formed
from $r$ and $s$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Binary dot product work]
\lean{FABL.executableBinaryDotProductWork}
\label{FABL.executableBinaryDotProductWork}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.binaryConstructorTraversalWork}
For a natural number $\ell$, define the work count to be the binary constructor traversal
work with parameter $2$ on the list of natural numbers from $0$ through $\ell-1$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Binary dot product work]
\lean{FABL.executableBinaryDotProductWork_eq}
\label{FABL.executableBinaryDotProductWork_eq}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.binaryConstructorTraversalWork_eq, FABL.executableBinaryDotProductWork}
\difficulty{1}
For every nonnegative integer $\ell$, the work assigned to the executable binary dot
product is $2\ell$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Executable work for a small-bias output bit]
\lean{FABL.executableSmallBiasOutputBitWork}
\label{FABL.executableSmallBiasOutputBitWork}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.executableBinaryDotProductWork, FABL.executableSmallBiasPowerWork}
For natural numbers $\ell$ and $c$, define the work required for output coordinate $c$
to be the executable small-bias power work at parameters $\ell$ and $c+1$, plus the
executable binary dot-product work at parameter $\ell$, plus one.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Output bit work identity]
\lean{FABL.executableSmallBiasOutputBitWork_eq}
\label{FABL.executableSmallBiasOutputBitWork_eq}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.binaryMulModWork, FABL.executableBinaryDotProductWork_eq, FABL.executableSmallBiasOutputBitWork, FABL.executableSmallBiasPowerWork_eq}
\difficulty{3}
For every pair of natural numbers $\ell$ and $j$, the work required for output bit $j$
equals $\ell+(j+1)(M(\ell)+1)+2\ell+1$, where $M(\ell)$ is the work for one binary
modular multiplication.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Output bit work bound]
\lean{FABL.executableSmallBiasOutputBitWork_le}
\label{FABL.executableSmallBiasOutputBitWork_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.binaryAddWork, FABL.binaryArithmeticWork_le, FABL.binaryMulModWork, FABL.executableSmallBiasOutputBitWork, FABL.executableSmallBiasOutputBitWork_eq}
\difficulty{5}
For all natural numbers $\ell$ and $j$, the work for output bit $j$ is at most
$16(j+1)(\ell+1)^2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Output bit specification and work bound]
\lean{FABL.executableSmallBiasOutputBit_spec}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p153-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p153-b004
}
\label{FABL.executableSmallBiasOutputBit_spec}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CertifiedBinaryFieldImplementation, FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.executableSmallBiasGenerator, FABL.executableSmallBiasOutputBit, FABL.executableSmallBiasOutputBitWork, FABL.executableSmallBiasOutputBitWork_le, FABL.executableSmallBiasOutputBit_eq_generator}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n,\ell\in\mathbb N$, with $\ell>0$, and let a certified binary field implementation
of degree $\ell$ and binary vectors $r,s$ of length $\ell$ be given. For every
coordinate $i<n$, the output bit at $i$ equals coordinate $i$ of the generator vector
formed from $r$ and $s$, and its work is at most $16(i+1)(\ell+1)^2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Joint output-bit work growth]
\lean{FABL.executableSmallBiasOutputBitWork_isBigO}
\label{FABL.executableSmallBiasOutputBitWork_isBigO}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.executableSmallBiasOutputBitWork, FABL.executableSmallBiasOutputBitWork_le}
\difficulty{3}
As $\ell$ and $j$ vary jointly over the natural numbers, the work for output bit $j$ is
$O((j+1)(\ell+1)^2)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Fixed-coordinate work growth]
\lean{FABL.executableSmallBiasOutputBitWork_fixedCoordinate_isBigO}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p166-b004}
\label{FABL.executableSmallBiasOutputBitWork_fixedCoordinate_isBigO}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.executableSmallBiasOutputBitWork, FABL.executableSmallBiasOutputBitWork_le}
\difficulty{3}
For every fixed natural-number coordinate $j$, the work for output bit $j$, as a
function of $\ell$, is $O((\ell+1)^2)$ as $\ell\to\infty$.
\end{theorem}
